shared_mechanisms: Four mechanisms are reused across my seven themes, and I designed each once. (M1) A canonical vocabulary package app/core/vocab/ (T01) owns stage, sector (two levels), BOM category, entry mode, reg subtype, idea type, health classification, language code and domain resolution, with one word-boundary cue matcher. T21 uses it to match founder context to news items, T26 uses its Language enum and script detector, and T31 uses Stage to place funding milestones and schemes. (M2) Declared derivation keys app/agents/keys.py (T06): every derived artefact (research, council, roadmap, narration marks) states the inputs it depends on, and its key is a hash of exactly those inputs. Results, jobs, narration and stored plans compare keys instead of positions or 'latest'. T11's fact pool admits only artefacts whose key is current, and T31's plan snapshot is keyed by plan_key. (M3) One append-only Turn record per founder turn in the session document (T11): founder text, tool rounds with result references, and reply sentences each carrying {text, language, origin, provider}. T26's per-sentence language and truthful provider attribution are fields of that record, not a second structure. (M4) The host-side scheduled job (5.4.4, OS scheduler) and the frozen migration chain (T16). T21's news corpus refresh and T26's voice-cache sweep are steps of the scheduled runner, and T31's plans table lands as an explicit migration on the chain T16 makes reliable.

designs.understanding: Every module that reasons about what kind of venture this is (stage, sector, BOM category, entry mode, registration subtype, idea type, domain, health) keeps its own string literals and its own substring cues. Nothing owns the meaning of these values, so a value produced in one vocabulary is compared with a literal from another and the comparison is silently False: 'revenue' is unknown to readiness (_STAGE_SCORE knows 'launched'/'scaling') and to investor stage maps; elicitation 'health' meets registry 'healthtech' in K_DOMAIN; the elicitation Sector enum (12), ecosystem SECTORS (20) and registry categories (12 StartupTN) disagree, so food/education/retail have no StartupTN home. Cue sets are duplicated and use raw substring tests ('iot' in 'patriot', 'smart' -> PCB). Two health classifiers and two domain resolvers give contradictory advice in one conversation. The root cause is the absence of a single owned module with explicit mappings and a test that fails on an unmapped value or a stray literal. I checked readiness.py:22, investors.py _STAGES, vote.py idea_type (health_bio checked first), slots.py Sector and EntryMode, models/enums.py EntryMode/RegSubtype, Funding.tsx/Profile.tsx/Schemes.tsx STAGE literals, journeyStore.ts EntryMode. All evidence holds. Additional finding: the elicitation 'stage' slot is declared kind='enum' but has no enum attached (slots.py), so stage is effectively free text there too.

flags_disputed.note: Holds, and worse than stated: the elicitation 'stage' slot has kind='enum' but enum=None, so the agent path stores free-text stage words that no consumer maps.

Holds. I disagree only with treating StartupTN categories as a level every consumer must carry; in my design the 20 ecosystem sectors are the single join key and the StartupTN category is a derived display label.

designs.chosen: Canonical vocabulary package (Python str Enums + explicit mapping tables + one cue matcher) with a literal-ban test and generated TypeScript
designs.why_chosen: It removes the root cause (no owner of meaning) rather than a symptom, it is deterministic and offline (0002), and it reuses what already exists: slots.Sector as an Enum, taxonomy.py's compiled cues and NIC tables, registry.detect_domain as the best-tested domain resolver (10/10 on the eval domain check). One matcher fixes the BOM and sector false hits at once; one domain resolver and one health classifier close the 'two doors' bugs (novelty vs council). The generated TS file costs about 40 lines of Python and no new npm dependency, and the AST test keeps the drift from coming back.

not_chosen.name: Per-module alias tables
not_chosen.reason: Patches each symptom and leaves seven vocabularies; the next new word breaks again and nothing can test coverage.

not_chosen.name: Data-file taxonomy loaded at runtime
not_chosen.reason: Reverts use sites to strings without static checking; the curated data (synonyms, NIC prefixes, labels) lives in Python tables next to the enums, which reviewers can read as easily.

not_chosen.name: OpenAPI-generated TypeScript types
not_chosen.reason: Only fixes the browser edge; the most damaging mismatches are in-process Python lookups. Worth doing later under 5.3.4; the vocab export covers the enums now without an npm dependency.

not_chosen.name: Learned classifier
not_chosen.reason: No labelled outcomes, not explainable, needs the network on the free path, and contradicts 0002 (code decides).

design.data_model: Session slots store canonical values: the sector slot holds a Sector member (primary); a derived, never-asked field sectors: list[Sector] holds every cue hit. The stage slot gets enum=Stage. Registry domain cards gain idea_type: IdeaType (curated in Git). AgentStartIn gains entry_mode: EntryMode | None and reg_subtype: RegSubtype | None (Pydantic validates; unknown -> 422). Session gains domain: str | None set by resolve_domain and re-resolved when the research key changes (T06). Old sessions: the 2.1.4 upgrade-on-read step maps legacy enum strings with to_sector/to_stage.
design.algorithm: Primary sector: prefer the founder's explicit answer; otherwise the cue hit with most matches, ties broken by first mention; if two sectors tie, slot confidence is lowered so the engine confirms (existing CONFIRMING state). Idea type precedence: (1) registry domain card idea_type when resolve_domain matched; (2) founder slots (sector + product_form), e.g. food -> food, healthtech + physical -> health_device; (3) scan categories only after the clinical gate is applied to categories too, as a last fallback. Investor match: eligible if founder Stage is in the union of ROUND_STAGES[r] for the investor's rounds. Readiness: product-stage score keyed by Stage with revenue/growth/scale above mvp, and 'Ship an MVP' advice only below mvp. BOM decompose: word-boundary matching against BomCategory synonyms, all hit categories kept (not first match); when nothing matches the result is 'unknown product: add the lines yourself' with no packaging default.
design.interfaces: T03 (slot validate-then-put) calls vocab.to_sector/to_stage as per-slot validators, so a value enters a slot only as a member. T06 uses resolve_domain's output as an input of the research key. T21 news FounderContext normalises sector with to_sector and matches items with the Sector cue table instead of a raw substring of the id. T26 uses Language and detect_script. T31 uses Stage to place funding milestones and annotate schemes. T04 (typed founder-facts contract) reads Stage/Sector members for scheme rules.

designs.understanding: Nothing declares which inputs a derived result depends on. idea_version hashes the lowercased text of five core slots, so filling sector or product_form (which research never reads) changes it (4 versions in a 7-turn interview), while lever choices that change the idea (localise, cost-down) do not. Levers have no id or patch and are tracked by list index; narration marks ('statement', 'lever:0', 'searching') are global and never cleared; jobs are keyed by (session, kind) with reuse_done; results are stored under LATEST; and s.roadmap, s.council and s.novelty are untagged single fields. The consequences: research re-runs too often if keyed by idea_version and never when it should if not; a new version's verdict is never spoken; panel reordering skips or repeats levers; a late old job overwrites a new view; the roadmap and panel stay on the old idea after a lever choice. I checked ideation.py (idea_version :136-142, _next_novelty_point :562-580, _absorb :418-449, _offline_stream :655+), jobs.py (start with reuse_done, LATEST), results.py (interface already keyed by idea_version but unused), novelty._levers (fixed kind order, plain text). All evidence holds.

approaches.name: Declared derivation keys (dependency manifest per artefact kind) with key-tagged results, jobs and narration
approaches.how: A module declares, for each artefact kind (research, council, roadmap), the exact inputs it reads; derive_key(kind, session) hashes those inputs. Results, jobs, narration marks and session artefacts carry the key they were built from; absorb and speak compare keys. Levers get stable content ids and a structured patch, and their wording is rendered at narration time.
approaches.basis: Content-addressed caching as in build systems (Bazel, Make), applied with hashlib and the ResultStore interface that already takes a version key
approaches.advantages: Re-runs exactly when the computation would differ; reverting to an earlier idea reuses its results; stale results can never be absorbed or spoken; one rule for every artefact
approaches.drawbacks: Inputs must be declared and kept truthful; a forgotten input makes a stale result look current

approaches.name: Monotonic generation counter per session
approaches.how: Bump an integer on every idea change and lever choice; tag results with it; drop older generations.
approaches.advantages: Trivial; always changes on a choice
approaches.drawbacks: Not content-based: undoing a lever discards valid results; filling an irrelevant slot still needs a rule for whether to bump

approaches.name: Re-run only after confirmation (state-machine gate)
approaches.how: Research runs once on the first clear idea and again only after the founder confirms a changed restatement.
approaches.drawbacks: A wrong early scan is narrated for the whole interview; lever choices after the roadmap still need artefact tagging

approaches.name: Debounce or change-magnitude threshold on idea text
approaches.how: Re-run when the version is stable for N turns or token Jaccard drops below a threshold.
approaches.drawbacks: Arbitrary constants; one-word changes like solar -> diesel matter; adds latency

approaches.name: Session versions[] history (fork per version)
approaches.how: Each idea version is a sub-document with its own slots, results and narration.
approaches.basis: Decision 0003 lets the document hold history
approaches.drawbacks: Larger documents and a heavier refactor before anyone needs history; does not by itself define which inputs matter

approaches.drawbacks: Does not fix keying; Redis is optional; belongs to 2.3.1

designs.chosen: Declared derivation keys (dependency manifest per artefact kind) with key-tagged results, jobs and narration
designs.why_chosen: The root cause is literally that nothing defines which inputs a result depends on; declaring them is the direct fix and answers every flag at once: filling sector no longer re-runs research (sector is not a research input), a lever patch that adds search terms does, a None key cannot exist once there is text, the board and the result store agree on a key, a late old result is rejected by key comparison, the roadmap and panel are stale exactly when their own inputs changed, and narration marks scoped by key make a new verdict audible. It needs only hashlib and the existing ResultStore interface, and it is the same mechanism T11 (facts from current artefacts) and T31 (plan snapshot keyed by plan_key) reuse.

not_chosen.name: Monotonic generation counter
not_chosen.reason: Not content-based: undoing a lever throws away identical results, and it still needs a rule for which changes bump it, which is the declaration this design makes anyway.

not_chosen.name: Re-run only after confirmation
not_chosen.reason: Leaves a wrong early verdict narrated through the whole interview and does nothing for post-roadmap lever choices.

not_chosen.name: Debounce or change-magnitude threshold
not_chosen.reason: Arbitrary constants that both delay real changes and miss one-word changes that matter.

not_chosen.name: Session versions[] history
not_chosen.reason: Storage growth and a refactor before any founder needs 'go back'; can be added later on top of keys (a version is a key plus its slot snapshot).

not_chosen.name: Durable queue with job ids
not_chosen.reason: Out of scope (2.3.1) and does not fix keying; the board keeps its in-process design (0010) with the new key.

design.algorithm: Each turn: compute keys. Research: if there is no current-key result and none running for that key, start a job for (session, research, key); a running job for a different research key is cancelled (cheap now that the key is stable). absorb takes only results whose key equals the current key; a late result for an old key stays in the store (reusable on undo) and is never applied. Council and roadmap: if the envelope key differs from the current derive_key, the artefact is stale: not spoken, not shown as current, the snapshot says 'out of date for your latest change'; the council is re-convened in the background; the roadmap is rebuilt on the next generate. Lever choice: apply the patch through T03's validated put (source LEVER) and append the id to chosen_levers; if the elicitation state is COMPLETE, move to CONFIRMING with a restatement of the changed slots only. Narration: the statement for the current research key once; then the panel's view; then levers in the panel's order (vote ranks all lever ids; fall back to novelty order), up to 3 per version, skipping ids already marked for this key. A 'what changed' line compares the previous and current statement when both exist.
design.interfaces: T03: lever patches and slot updates go through the validated put with a LEVER source rank. T01: domain from resolve_domain is a key input; lever phrase tables keyed by Sector. T11: the fact pool includes only envelopes whose key is current; tool results in turns reference results by (kind, key). T31: plan_key is the roadmap envelope key and the plans-table snapshot key; statuses reconcile across plan keys. Council (1.3.1): ranks levers by id; the prior-art seat's variant is chosen after scoring, not as lever 0.

designs.understanding: AgentSession.messages is three things at once: the resume transcript (snapshot reads string messages), the provider context (sent whole each turn) and the grounding pool (_facts flattens every tool_result and founder string ever appended into one set of bare numbers). It has no turn boundaries (a turn adds up to 2*(MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS+1)+1 messages), stores full tool payloads that duplicate s.scan/s.roadmap/s.novelty, and the system prompt interpolates founder-supplied name and known facts plus the per-turn question and news, so neither caching nor injection safety is possible. Any trim breaks the fact check or resume; any summary either launders model text into facts or is dropped; the fact pool grows weaker as the session grows (a roadmap's 25 backs '25 lakh'). I checked ideation.py SYSTEM (:66-110), _facts (:278-302), _llm_stream (:482-551), snapshot (:226-250), grounding.facts_from/problems, providers._usage (input/output only). Evidence holds; one note: grounding.BANNED already replaces 'unique/novel' claims with the caveat, so F-B1-032's backstop option exists today.

Its second option, a novelty-claim rule in the fact check, already exists: grounding.BANNED maps 'unique', 'novel', 'first of its kind' (and Tamil/Hindi forms) to NOVELTY_LINE. The design keeps it and adds injection fixtures to its tests.

designs.understanding: The migration chain is not a frozen, self-contained history. 0001 imports app.models.Base and runs create_all for four tables, so its effect changes whenever the models change and a later add_column migration fails with DuplicateColumn on fresh databases. 0003 imports pgvector at module level and creates the vector extension and an HNSW index for an embeddings table that no code reads and whose feature is Dropped, so a stock PostgreSQL 18 on the owner's machine fails at 0003 and 0004 (agent_sessions) never applies. The integration tests bypass the chain with create_all on the developer database and turn any setup error into a skip, and CI has no database at all, so none of this is ever seen. I checked 0001_initial.py, 0003_embeddings.py, 0004 down_revision, env.py (no URL override), the test_agent_store.py fixture, ci.yml, models/__init__.py and pyproject (pgvector dependency). All evidence holds.

designs.understanding: Two faults share one cause: the voice layer does not know what kind of sentence it is speaking. (1) Speech output: /speak tries Gemini before the free local recordings, caches every synthesised sentence by a hash of its text forever (including restatements of the founder's idea), so a deleted conversation survives as audio that cannot be found by session; grouped multi-sentence requests can never match per-sentence recordings, so a 429 means silence. (2) Language: there is one language tag per reply and per session, set only when the client sends one; typed Tamil or Hindi never sets it; about half of offline sentences have translations, so replies mix languages under one tag; and translated fixed sentences increment the 'reworded' counter, so the done event names a model provider that was never called (which would also trigger the Gemini data notice wrongly). I checked routers/voice.py (Gemini first, write-through cache, phrasebook only after), phrasebook.translation (exact match), ideation.py turn_stream (language only from the request) and _reword_stream (translations counted as reworded, provider set). All evidence holds.

designs.understanding: The planner produces a good deterministic plan but treats it as a transient reply: it lives only in s.roadmap inside a session that hides after 6 idle hours, so a months-long tracker has nothing to track; confidence is a fixed 0.8 default (tools._roadmap never passes it) and only months_realistic is spoken, so the restatement's promise to widen estimates is false; milestones whose applies condition is unknown are silently dropped (text-only Ideate calls lose funding and compliance steps), so Ideate and Talk differ; pack templates override common ids with different meanings (c_pilot, c_customers) while the tracker keys status by bare id; status ignores depends_on and the critical path; and c_grant sits in Growth after c_pilot although the domain's own scheme routes are prototype grants. I checked plan.py (_templates override by id, confidence=0.8), roadmap.py (sigma from confidence, per-milestone bands only, no band totals), common.json (c_grant phase Growth depends_on c_pilot), tools._roadmap and the Ideate.tsx tracker. All evidence holds.

designs.chosen: Durable plan snapshot keyed by plan_key with content-addressed milestone uids, tri-state applicability, coverage-based confidence and a server 'remaining' function
designs.why_chosen: It treats the roadmap as what the founder tracks for months: a stored, versioned artefact, separate from the transcript. It reuses T06's derivation key (plan_key) so a snapshot is current exactly when its inputs are, T16's frozen chain for the plans migration, T01's Stage to place funding milestones and schemes, and the planner's own graph code for the remaining path. Each flag is fixed in the right layer: sequencing in reviewed pack data, unknowns and confidence in the planner, identity in uids, durability in the plans row, progress in one server function that the tracker and the cohort both read.

design.components: planner/data/packs/common.json: c_grant split into c_seed_grant (phase Validation, depends_on c_define, applies funding_route in grant/mixed; prototype milestones in packs depend on it) and c_growth_funding (phase Growth, depends_on c_pilot); c_loan and c_equity keep stage-appropriate placement; each funding template declares target_stages: [Stage]. schemes/annotate.py: a scheme goes on the funding milestone whose target_stages contain the scheme's target Stage (T01), not by phase. planner evaluate(): tri-state (true, false, unknown); unknown keeps the milestone with conditional: {slot, label}, excluded from the critical-path total and listed in next_questions. Confidence: planner_confidence(slots) = mean over the planner's required slots of slot confidence (0 when missing or skipped, from T03's typed slot values), floored at 0.3, passed by tools._roadmap; build returns months_optimistic and months_pessimistic summed along the critical path; _roadmap_line says 'about N months, between A and B'. Milestone uid = pack:template_id:sha1(title, depends_on, effort_weeks)[:8]. planner/progress.py (new): remaining(plan, statuses) -> {open_critical_path, months_remaining (realistic/optimistic/pessimistic), warnings: milestones done while a dependency is not done} using the existing graph functions; reconcile(old_plan, old_statuses, new_plan) -> statuses carried when uids are equal or when template id and title are equal (marked carried), the rest kept in history. Plans store: models/plan.py and migration 0006_plans: id, owner_id (users FK, nullable for anonymous until T30/3.1.1), session_id, idea_version, plan_key, pack_id, domain, plan JSONB, statuses JSONB, history JSONB, created_at, superseded_by; written when the founder confirms (generate) and when a rebuild after a lever choice produces a new plan_key (old row superseded, statuses reconciled). Anonymous sessions keep the snapshot envelope in the session and it is promoted to a plans row on sign-in or 'save this idea' (2.1.3.2). Routes: GET /ideation/agent/sessions/{id}/plan, PATCH status by uid, GET remaining. Ideate.tsx reads the session's plan (no text-only build). cohort/programme.py: progress band from plan statuses, folded below 5 founders.
design.data_model: plans table as above; statuses: {uid: {state: not_started|in_progress|done, at}}. Session envelope: {key: plan_key, data: plan} per T06.
design.algorithm: remaining: done set D; open graph = milestones not in D; critical path over the open graph by realistic months (existing function); totals for the three bands; a warning for each done milestone with a dependency not in D (warn, never block). The 0.3 confidence floor maps to sigma 0.62 in roadmap.months.
design.interfaces: T06: plan_key = derive_key('roadmap', s); stale when it differs. T30/3.1.1: owner_id FK and erasure (3.2.4 deletes plans with the founder); retention rule separate from sessions. T04: scheme annotation reads typed founder facts. T01: Stage for target_stages and schemes. T16: migration 0006 on the frozen chain, covered by CI. 1.4.3: the plan is built from session slots only.
